RoomType.maps_to: RoomType.Monster (SeapunkNormal.cs:10). Sim equivalent: 'seapunk_normal' is listed in ActRooms.normal_keys for underdocks (rooms.py:199-203), the structural stand-in for RoomType.Monster -- it also drives the MinGoldReward/MaxGoldReward ladder (see guards) via CombatState.room_type, set at combat creation from the same pool membership (run.py, unhashed -- see extra_sources note).

Tags.maps_to: EncounterTag.Seapunk (SeapunkNormal.cs:12). Sim: ActRooms.tags['seapunk_normal'] = ('seapunk',) (rooms.py:214), matching 'seapunk_weak' (rooms.py:213) so the two never repeat back-to-back. The tag lives on the room-layer registry rather than on the Encounter object itself (Encounter has no tags field, monsters/base.py:353-381); the picker mechanism that consumes it (GrabBag-style no-repeat-tag selection) is seam/rooms_and_map's subject, not re-verdicted here -- only the VALUE is checked and it matches.

AllPossibleMonsters.maps_to: [Seapunk, CalcifiedCultist] (SeapunkNormal.cs:14-18). Its only two C# consumers are NBestiary.cs:194 (the Bestiary screen) and ActModel.AllMonsters/ModelDb.Monsters (ActModel.cs:169, ModelDb.cs:177 -- asset-preload dedup across an act), both presentation/infrastructure with no headless equivalent. The sim's nearest functional analog is full_env.py's global MONSTER_IDS vocabulary (full_env.py:252-269), which enumerates every registered Monster subclass regardless of per-encounter membership, so nothing an observation could need is missing for want of a per-encounter AllPossibleMonsters.
AllPossibleMonsters.rationale: Bestiary display and asset preload have no headless counterpart in this sim; the global MONSTER_IDS vocabulary already makes every monster identity representable, so the narrower per-encounter listing costs nothing observable.

GenerateMonsters.maps_to: SeapunkNormal.cs:20-27 returns [(CalcifiedCultist, null), (Seapunk, null)] -- 2 monsters, cultist first, both unslotted, 0 Rng draws. Sim: seapunk.py:67-70, Encounter(id='seapunk_normal', monster_classes=[CalcifiedCultist, Seapunk]) -- same 2 classes in the same order, 0 draws (Encounter.create_monsters, monsters/base.py:476-479, only rolls each monster's per-instance HP off the shared combat rng, mirroring CombatState.CreateCreature's parity Niche roll, not a GenerateMonsters-level draw -- the C# body itself calls no Rng method). Roster, order, slot-nullness and draw count (0) all match element-for-element.

ShouldReceiveCombatHooks.maps_to: EncounterModel.cs:39, `=> false`. Sim: Encounter instances are never registered with HookSystem -- CombatState.__init__ (combat.py:124-239) registers the player, every deck card (plus its affliction/enchantment), and every Monster (Monster.__init__, monsters/base.py:296-297), but never `self.encounter` (assigned bare at combat.py:239). The encounter is not a hook listener in either implementation.
